newsitem.title: UK: Philippines rating upgrade gives Bradys a fillip.
newsitem.headline: Philippines rating upgrade gives Bradys a fillip.

text.p: The Brady market saw active two-way trade in Philippine debt following the upgrade by international ratings agency Standard & Poor's Corp, traders said.
The Philippines welcomed the news that its sovereign rating had been upgraded by Standard & Poor's by one notch, bringing it closer to investment grade.

Officials and analysts said the news was expected and its immediate impact would be to improve the pricing of the Philippine Central Bank's maiden Yankee bond issue which is set to be launched in the second quarter.
The Central Bank expects to issue bonds worth $750 million to $1.0 billion.
Standard & Poor's Corp said it had raised its rating on the Philippines' long-term foreign currency debt to BB-plus from BB.
A similar upgrade is also expected soon from Moody's Investors Service Inc which announced three weeks ago that it was reviewing the Philippines for a possible upgrade.

The Philippines is optimistic that it can exit 34 years of IMF supervision this year when it expedites the passage into law of the remaining portion of its comprehensive tax reform package that will provide a solid revenue base for the government.
At 1000 GMT Philippine Pars PH425L18=RR bonds were bid at 90-1/8, up 1/8 point amid good two-way trade, dealers said.
Russian Minfins saw some light selling amid speculation the government would supply more Minfin bonds, dealers said.
"Russian Minfin 4's and 5's have seen some selling," a dealer said.
Russian Minfin 4 was bid at 63-1/2, unchanged from the previous close. The Russian Minfin 5 was bid at 44-5/8, also unchanged from the previous close.

Dealers said Brazilian Brady prices were still waiting for direction after confusion on implications of the wage ruling by Brazil's supreme court. The benchmark Brazil C bonds were 1/8 point up at 80-1/2 bid.
There was also a strong bid for Ecuador, they said, citing the 1/8 gain on the Ecuador pars bid at 46-5/8.
Ecuador extending its bridge loan to six months from one month, giving the President Alarcon's government more breathing space, gave its bonds a lift, New York traders said.
Dealers said rumours of a 10-year Eurobond issue for Venezuela was boosting the bid for the Brady debt.
The Venezuela Pars bonds were unchanged at 1030 GMT at 78-3/8 bid.
